name: What is a 'rough-in' and why is it important for toilet replacement?

mainEntity.name: What is a 'rough-in' and why is it important for toilet replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: A toilet's 'rough-in' refers to the distance from the finished wall behind the toilet to the center of the drainpipe (flange) in the floor. Standard rough-in measurements are 12 inches, but 10-inch and 14-inch options also exist. Knowing your rough-in measurement is crucial when selecting a new toilet, as it ensures the new fixture will fit correctly. Our plumbers can measure your existing rough-in to help you choose a compatible toilet for your remodel in Goodyear or Buckeye.
acceptedAnswer.description: Rough-in is the distance from the wall to the drainpipe center. It's critical for selecting a new toilet that fits your bathroom.
